newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire's ex-foreign minister alive - news agency.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's ex-foreign minister alive - news agency.

text.p: Zaire's ex-Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda, who diplomats feared had been shot dead on Saturday while trying to leave the country, is alive in Togo's capital Lome, Belgian news agency Belga said on Sunday.
Belga said it had spoken to Kamanda by telephone.
Western diplomats in Zaire's capital Kinshasa said on Saturday they feared Kamanda had been killed by one of his bodyguards as he tried to leave the city by boat to neighbouring Congo.

But Kamanda told Belga he had not been in Kinshasa at the time. He said he left for Togo from the Congolese port of Pointe-Noire, where he had accompanied Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko earlier in the week for aborted talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
Kabila proclaimed victory in Zaire's seven-month civil war on Saturday and Mobutu has fled to Morocco.
Kamanda, who was also deputy prime minister, was at the forefront of Mobutu's team in negotiations with the rebels.
He told Belga he was uncertain about his future but had not ruled out returning to Zaire.
